statement: Ana, Bo and Cal sit on a bench with 4 seats, so one seat stays empty. In how many different ways can they sit?

choices.misconception: I only counted which seat stays empty and forgot the children can swap places.
I only counted the orders of the three children and forgot the empty seat can move.
I thought the empty seat had to be at one of the two ends.
I gave each child 4 choices of seat, letting two children share a seat.

hints: Let the children choose seats one at a time.
Ana picks a seat first, then Bo picks from the seats left, then Cal. Multiply the numbers of choices, remembering that a seat cannot be used twice.
Ana has 4 seats to choose from, then Bo has 3 and Cal has 2.

solutions.reliable: Ana can take any of the 4 seats, Bo any of the 3 left and Cal any of the 2 left, so 4 x 3 x 2 = 24 ways. The transferable idea: when people choose places one after another, the number of choices drops by one each time.
solutions.elegant: Choose the empty seat (4 ways), then arrange the three children in the other three seats (3 x 2 x 1 = 6 ways): 4 x 6 = 24. The transferable idea: treat the empty seat as a fourth, invisible person.

whyOnTest: Arrangements with more places than people, where both the empty seat and the order of the children must be counted.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
